object_description: stepped three-story volume with terraces and veranda layers
design_condition: The building is inserted between the existing school buildings to form a new small place, with a covered connection framing the space; its eastern height follows the existing eaves while the western setback responds to smaller neighboring buildings.

positive.statement: The idea of creating a new small place between the two buildings is convincing.

position.target: new small place between two buildings
position.rationale: Central interstitial space is suggested by stepped massing and open breaks in the elevations.

positive.statement: The volumetric staggering and resulting terraces and veranda layers give the classrooms a new quality and make a valuable pedagogical contribution.

position.target: volumetric staggering, terraces, and veranda layers
position.rationale: Setbacks and repeated horizontal layers are clearly visible along the elongated upper volume.

positive.statement: The directly adjacent outdoor spaces have the potential to become a real green classroom.

position.rationale: Adjacent outdoor teaching space is placed beside the building’s lower, setback side.

positive.statement: The filigree facade and veranda layer establish a relationship with the existing school building.

position.rationale: Layered facade and veranda expression are most legible on the long elevation faces.

negative.statement: The design of the light, delicate covered connection remains questionable.

position.rationale: Covered connection is not separately identifiable; approximate it along the central access-side edge.

negative.statement: The narrow, elongated auditorium-library combination is assessed critically.

position.rationale: The elongated building footprint supports a constrained room anchor toward its rear half.

negative.statement: The daylight provided only by skylights in the basement workroom is insufficient.

position.rationale: Basement skylights are not directly resolved; place them near the central lower-floor surface.

negative.statement: The different staircases create cramped spatial situations and make the corridor zone implausible as an expanded teaching area.

position.rationale: Internal circulation is unobservable; the central stacked zone is the most plausible approximation.

negative.statement: The building has the largest floor area and building volume among the projects judged in the final round.

position.target: largest floor area and building volume
position.rationale: Comparative area and volume are whole-building judgments without a unique spatial point.

negative.statement: The building shell is only average in terms of compactness.

position.rationale: Shell compactness is a global performance judgment rather than a localized feature.
